entities.summary:
The 2019 United Kingdom general election was a pivotal event in British politics, occurring on December 12, 2019, and determining the composition of the 58th House of Commons.

The election saw a significant shift in the country's political landscape, with the Conservative Party, led by Boris Johnson, securing a majority of 80 seats, while the Labour Party, led by Jeremy Corbyn, suffered a significant defeat.

The 2019 United Kingdom general election had far-reaching consequences, including the passage of the Brexit Withdrawal Agreement and the UK's ultimate departure from the European Union on January 31, 2020.

One notable outcome of the election was the solidification of the Conservative Party's position as the dominant force in British politics, paving the way for Johnson's subsequent dissolution of Parliament and the call for a new election in December 2019.

In the words of historian and journalist, Robert Peston, 'The 2019 election was a wake-up call for the Labour Party, a reminder that the British people had lost faith in their ability to govern the country effectively.'
